modern: Judge every word and deed that is according to nature to be fit for you; and do not be turned aside by the blame that follows from anyone, nor by their words, but if a thing is good to be done or said, do not consider it unworthy of you. For those people have their own leading principle and follow their own impulse; pay no attention to these things, but go straight on, following your own nature and the common nature; and the way of both is one.
original: Judge every word and deed which are according to nature to be fit for thee; and be not diverted by the blame which follows from any people, nor by their words, but if a thing is good to be done or said, do not consider it unworthy of thee. For those persons have their peculiar leading principle and follow their peculiar movement; which things do not thou regard, but go straight on, following thy own nature and the common nature; and the way of both is one.

explained.summary:
If something is right to do or say, do it, and don’t let criticism put you off. Other people’s comments come from their own minds and impulses, which are theirs to manage, not yours.

Keep going straight ahead, following your own nature and the nature of the whole, meaning the way the universe works and your part in it. For Marcus these two paths are really one: what’s good for you as a reasonable, sociable being is what fits the world.
explained.today: Speaking up in a meeting when something isn’t right, or choosing to cycle to work while friends tease you about it. If you’re confident it’s the right thing, the eye-rolls and the sarcastic comment in the group chat are theirs to deal with.
